analysis.title: The Good the Bad and the Ugly for Rates in 2027
key_insights: ING's US baseline has three obstacles (AI-driven productivity as the 'good', elevated fiscal deficits as the 'bad', renewed inflation from ongoing wars as the 'ugly') pushing the 10yr US Treasury yield back to the 5.25%-plus area through at least Q1 2027, versus 4.9% currently.
ING caps the 10yr UST upside at 5.5%. Later in 2027 it expects 2%-plus GDP growth, falling inflation and a stable but not worsening debt dynamic.
Falling US inflation is the key variable. It lets the Federal Reserve step away and the market re-discount cuts, so the 10yr targets 4.75% first and likely settles in a 4.5-4.75% zone.
A decision to materially cut long-end Treasury funding would push long yields lower. ING does not forecast it.
Euro rates face a bumpy start to 2027 as markets weigh each inflation reading for second-round effects. If inflation eases, the 2yr EUR swap rate falls about 50bp on a repricing of the ECB path.
The 10yr EUR swap rate is stickier because a global rise in real rates pushes longer euro rates up. If inflation does not ease, the 10yr swap rate could go well above 4%.

Eurozone bonds are tested by fiscal strains and election risk. France is the key fault line, and Bunds' safe-haven appeal masks mounting supply pressure. ING expects a turbulent H1 2027, with relief dependent on a credible French fiscal consolidation path.

GBP rates are well above ING's fair value, but investors remain wary of the Bank of England turning dovish too quickly. ING pencils in a significant repricing lower only once the BoE shows it can bring inflation closer to target by end-2027.
The GBP path lower will not be smooth because of high sensitivity to US rates. Gilt markets increasingly rely on risk-sensitive investors, so ING sees a material term risk premium as justified.

Almost €900bn of Dutch pension assets are scheduled to transition to the new system in January 2027. ING expects this to keep the 10s30s euro swap curve structurally steeper, though macro remains the main curve driver for now.
Under the new Dutch system ING expects more swap flows through the year, as interest rate hedging needs move with asset prices such as equities.

Pressure from AI productivity, fiscal deficits and war-driven inflation pushes long yields higher.
Falling inflation lets the Fed step away and the market re-price cuts, so long yields ease.

Reflects a significant repricing of the ECB path if inflation eases.

risk_factors: Inflation fails to ease, which would push euro and US rates higher.
Elevated fiscal deficits and supply pressure, especially in France and Germany.
BoE credibility on inflation and gilt reliance on risk-sensitive investors.
Global rise in real rates pushing long euro rates up.
vol_and_positioning: Dutch pension reforms are expected to bring more swap flows through 2027, as hedging needs move with asset prices such as equities.
geopolitical: Ongoing wars are cited as the source of renewed inflationary pressure.
French fiscal consolidation and eurozone election risk are named as pressure points for European bond spreads.

tension_points.bull_case: By mid-2027 inflation falls, growth holds at 2%-plus and the debt dynamic is stable but not worsening. The Fed steps away, the market re-discounts cuts and the 10yr settles at 4.5-4.75%.
tension_points.bear_case: AI productivity, fiscal deficits and war-driven inflation push the 10yr to 5.25%-plus, capped at 5.5%, through at least Q1 2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation failing to fall by mid-2027 would block the Fed stepping away and the repricing of cuts.

tension_points.bull_case: Inflation eases and the ECB path reprices significantly, taking the 2yr EUR swap rate down about 50bp.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation does not ease as hoped and the 10yr swap rate could push well above 4%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Inflation readings showing second-round effects would invalidate the easing path.
